trust_decision.summary: On a redirect, sensitive credential headers (authorization, cookie, proxy-authorization) must not be carried to a different origin; the decision is made in Client._request while building redirectOptions, and is keyed on hostname only instead of scheme+host+port.

landing_point.why: The comment 'When redirecting to a new hostname, remove sensitive credential headers' and the hostname comparison two lines below are the only place the advisory summary points at; the whole redirect decision lives in Client._request.

fix_sites.entry_point: Wreck.request() (lib/index.js:56) via Client.request(); the get/post/patch/put/delete shortcuts (lib/index.js:522-545) and any client built by defaults() (lib/index.js:48-54) all delegate to this same call
fix_sites.module_kind: core HTTP client library, redirect handling inside Client._request

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No O2 site or O8 route exists; the only available argument is textual: the code comment and the existing test name say 'hostname' (lib/index.js:252, test/index.js:445), so a solver could read port and scheme changes as 'not a new host' and leave the check as it is.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A sensitive header must still be forwarded on a genuine same-origin redirect (relative Location '/'), so an over-broad fix that deletes the headers on every redirect breaks intended behaviour

O6_input_shapes: different hostname (behaviour already covered by the pinned test at test/index.js:411)
relative Location resolved against the current URL (lib/index.js:239-241)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: clear URL-embedded Basic credentials (options.auth / userinfo) on a cross-origin redirect, next to the header strip
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The same secret reaches the wire two ways in this file: as a sensitive header set (lib/index.js:23) and as uri.auth derived from URL userinfo (lib/index.js:677-681); a maintainer tightening credential handling could plausibly add the second check in applyUrlToOptions.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: re-apply the sensitive-header strip after the user beforeRedirect hook mutates redirectOptions, before followRedirect
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: beforeRedirect is documented as 'changes to this object are applied to the redirection request' (API.md:104) and runs after the strip, so a maintainer adding a recomposition guard there is a natural sibling of the same mechanism.

O9_family: CWE-522/CWE-200: insufficiently protected credentials / information exposure via credential headers crossing an origin boundary on redirect

O10_build.toolchain: npm; @hapi/lab test runner, script `lab -t 100 -L -a @hapi/code -m 10000 -Y`; no compile step
O10_build.project_tests: test/index.js: redirect header handling at test/index.js:411 (cross-host strip) and test/index.js:445 (same-host preserve); tests start local http and self-signed https servers on 127.0.0.1, so no external network is needed

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Compare uri.host (host+port) instead of uri.hostname: it passes both tests the fix adds (the scheme test uses different hostnames) while leaving a same-host, same-port scheme change open.

out_of_scope_notes: rejectUnauthorized is cloned into redirectOptions (lib/index.js:243) and re-selects the allow-unauthorized agent (lib/index.js:170-174), so a cross-scheme redirect can silently keep TLS verification off; outside this advisory's credential-header property, not pursued.
